title: Eltrombopag Plus Telitacicept vs. Eltrombopag Alone for Steroid-refractory/Relapsed ITP
off: Eltrombopag Combined With Telitacicept Versus Eltrombopag Monotherapy for the Treatment of Immune Thrombocytopenia Refractory or Relapsed to Corticosteroid Therapy: A Randomized Exploratory, Controlled, Open-label, Phase II Clinical Study
sponsor: Institute of Hematology & Blood Diseases Hospital, China
summary:
Background: Immune thrombocytopenia (ITP) is an autoimmune bleeding disorder. Corticosteroids are first-line therapy, but about one-third of patients relapse or are refractory. Eltrombopag (a TPO-RA) promotes platelet production, yet some patients show no response or relapse upon discontinuation. Telitacicept, a TACI-Fc fusion protein, dual-targets BAFF and APRIL, inhibiting B cell and plasma cell function and reducing autoantibody production, potentially providing synergistic immunomodulatory benefit.

Objective: To evaluate the sustained response rate of eltrombopag plus telitacicept vs. eltrombopag alone in patients with steroid-refractory/relapsed ITP.

Design: Randomized, open-label, controlled, exploratory Phase II study. 40 patients planned (20 combination, 20 monotherapy). Combination group: eltrombopag + telitacicept . Monotherapy group: eltrombopag alone for 12 weeks. Monotherapy patients with no response after 4 weeks may cross over to the combination group. After 12 weeks, treatment is stopped and patients are followed until Week 24.

Primary endpoint: Proportion of patients maintaining platelet count ≥30×10⁹/L with no bleeding at 24 weeks post-treatment. Secondary endpoints include platelet response rates during 12 weeks, safety, bleeding events, etc.

Expected results: The combination group is expected to have a significantly higher proportion of patients achieving the primary endpoint without increased adverse events.

Population: Age ≥18, diagnosed ITP ≥3 months, baseline platelets \<30×10⁹/L, prior corticosteroid failure.

Safety: Monitoring for bleeding, infection, thrombosis, cytopenia, etc., with dose adjustment/cessation as per protocol.

Conclusion: This study explores whether dual-targeting (platelet production + autoimmune suppression) with eltrombopag and telitacicept can provide more durable remission for steroid-refractory/relapsed ITP patients.
elig:
Inclusion Criteria:

1. Age ≥18 years, regardless of sex.
2. Clinically diagnosed with immune thrombocytopenia for at least 3 months prior to enrollment. Platelet count \<30×10⁹/L within 48 hours before the first dose of study drug.
3. Previous failure (ineffective, unable to maintain response, or relapse) to first-line standard corticosteroid therapy for ITP as recommended by guidelines.
4. Any prior emergency treatment for ITP (e.g., corticosteroids, platelet transfusion, intravenous immunoglobulin) must have been completed at least 2 weeks before the first dose.
5. Patients receiving maintenance corticosteroid therapy must be on a stable dose for at least 2 weeks prior to the first dose; patients receiving immunosuppressants (e.g., azathioprine, danazol, cyclosporine A, tacrolimus, sirolimus, etc.) must be on a stable dose for at least 4 weeks prior to the first dose; anti-CD20 antibody therapy must have been completed \>3 months prior.

Understand the study procedures and voluntarily provide written informed consent.

Exclusion Criteria:

1. Received anti-CD20 antibody therapy within 3 months.
2. Uncontrolled primary disease of vital organs, such as malignant tumors, liver failure, heart failure, renal failure, etc.
3. Positive for HIV.
4. Uncontrolled active viral or bacterial infections, including positive for hepatitis B, hepatitis C, cytomegalovirus, Epstein-Barr virus, or syphilis.
5. Extensive and severe bleeding, such as hemoptysis, upper gastrointestinal hemorrhage, intracranial hemorrhage, etc.
6. Currently have cardiac disease requiring treatment, arrhythmia, or hypertension poorly controlled as judged by the investigator.
7. Patients with thrombotic diseases such as pulmonary embolism, thrombosis, atherosclerosis, etc.
8. Patients with mental disorders who are unable to give informed consent or undergo study procedures and follow-up normally.
9. Patients whose toxic symptoms from prior treatment before enrollment have not yet resolved.
10. Other serious diseases that may limit the patient's participation in this study (e.g., poorly controlled diabetes; severe cardiac insufficiency; myocardial infarction, unstable arrhythmia, or unstable angina within the past 6 months; gastric ulcer; active autoimmune disease, etc.).
11. Pregnant women, suspected pregnancy (positive urinary human chorionic gonadotropin pregnancy test at screening), or lactating patients.

x.titre: Eltrombopag plus télitacicept ou eltrombopag seul dans le PTI en échec des corticoïdes
x.question: Ajouter le télitacicept à l'eltrombopag augmente-t-il la proportion de patients gardant des plaquettes ≥ 30 G/L sans saignement 24 semaines après le traitement ?
x.contexte:
Le PTI est une maladie auto-immune hémorragique. Les corticoïdes sont le traitement de première ligne, mais environ un tiers des patients rechutent ou sont réfractaires. L'eltrombopag, agoniste du récepteur de la TPO, stimule la production plaquettaire, mais certains patients ne répondent pas et la rechute à l'arrêt est fréquente.

Le télitacicept est une protéine de fusion TACI-Fc qui bloque BAFF et APRIL, deux cytokines qui soutiennent la survie des lymphocytes B et des plasmocytes. Il pourrait réduire la production d'autoanticorps et compléter l'effet de l'eltrombopag. Cet essai exploratoire de phase II randomisé ouvert, mené à Tianjin (Institute of Hematology & Blood Diseases Hospital), inclut 40 adultes (20 par groupe) avec un PTI de plus de 3 mois, des plaquettes < 30 G/L et un échec des corticoïdes. Le traitement dure 12 semaines, suivi jusqu'à la semaine 24 ; les patients du bras eltrombopag sans réponse à 4 semaines peuvent passer dans le bras combiné.
x.interet: Les résultats indiqueront si un double ciblage (production plaquettaire et auto-immunité) donne des rémissions plus durables après l'arrêt du traitement.
x.profil: Des adultes ayant un PTI de plus de 3 mois, plaquettes < 30 G/L, après échec ou rechute des corticoïdes.
inclusion: PTI diagnostiqué depuis au moins 3 mois, plaquettes < 30 G/L dans les 48 heures avant la première dose
Échec, rechute ou perte de réponse aux corticoïdes de première ligne
Traitement de secours (corticoïdes, transfusion, immunoglobulines) terminé depuis au moins 2 semaines
Corticoïdes stables 2 semaines, immunosuppresseurs stables 4 semaines, anti-CD20 terminé depuis plus de 3 mois
exclusion: Maladie d'organe vital non contrôlée (cancer, insuffisance hépatique, cardiaque ou rénale)
VIH, infection virale ou bactérienne active non contrôlée (hépatites B et C, CMV, EBV, syphilis)
Saignement extensif et sévère (hémoptysie, hémorragie digestive haute, intracrânienne)
Cardiopathie nécessitant un traitement, arythmie ou hypertension mal contrôlée
Autre maladie sévère (diabète mal contrôlé, infarctus dans les 6 mois, maladie auto-immune active)

bras.traitement: Eltrombopag pendant 12 semaines ; passage possible dans le bras combiné en l'absence de réponse à 4 semaines

x.duree: 24 semaines (12 semaines de traitement puis suivi sans traitement)
x.critere: Proportion de patients avec plaquettes ≥ 30 G/L et sans saignement à 24 semaines après la première dose
